overview.description: Hokm (meaning 'Command' or 'Order') is Iran's most popular trick-taking card game. A partnership game for 4 players where the Hâkem (Ruler) declares trump after seeing only 5 cards. Teams compete to win 7 tricks per hand and 7 points to win the match. Play proceeds anticlockwise.

history.origins: Believed to be a descendant of ancient Persian card games, closely related to Court Piece (Coat Piece) played in South Asia. Its current form stabilized with standard French/English decks in the 19th-20th centuries.
timeline: 19th Century: Trick-taking games with trump calling become established in Persia.
20th Century: Becomes the de facto national card game of Iran.
Present: Exceptionally popular across generations, played in cafes, homes, and digitally.
history.evolution: Hokm refined the trump-calling mechanic where a single player (the Hâkem) is tasked with leading the team's strategy by choosing trump based on only their first 5 cards.
history.cultural: An essential part of Iranian social gatherings. Known for high-speed play and unspoken communication between partners.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite each other).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ranking: Ace (high) down to 2 (low) in all suits.
setup.dealing: To determine the first Hâkem, deal cards face-up one at a time anticlockwise until someone receives an Ace — they become Hâkem. For play: the player to Hâkem's right deals. First deal 5 cards to each player. Hâkem looks at 5 cards and declares trump. Then deal remaining 8 cards to each player (13 total).

rules.objective: Win tricks as a partnership. First team to win 7 tricks in a hand scores points. First team to accumulate 7 match points wins.
rules.gameplay:
1. HÂKEM SELECTION: Deal cards face-up anticlockwise until someone gets an Ace — they are the Hâkem (Ruler).
2. DEALING: Player to Hâkem's right deals 5 cards to each player anticlockwise.
3. TRUMP DECLARATION: Hâkem looks at 5 cards and declares the trump suit (Hokm). Hâkem must not show cards to anyone.
4. REMAINING DEAL: Dealer deals remaining 8 cards to each player (13 total per player).
5. TRICK PLAY: Hâkem leads the first trick. Play proceeds anticlockwise. Each player plays one card.
6. FOLLOWING SUIT: Must follow the suit led if possible. If void, may play any card including trump.
7. TRICK WINNER: Highest trump wins. If no trump played, highest card of the led suit wins. Winner leads next trick.
8. HAND SCORING: Team that wins 7+ out of 13 tricks wins the hand. Score: 1 point normally, 2 points for a slam (7-0). Some play Kot (all 13 tricks) = 3 points.
9. HÂKEM ROTATION: If Hâkem's team wins, Hâkem stays. If they lose, the player to Hâkem's right becomes the new Hâkem.
10. MATCH END: First team to 7 match points wins.
keyRules: Must follow suit if possible. If void in the led suit, any card may be played including trump.
Hâkem declares trump after seeing only their first 5 cards.
Highest trump wins the trick. If no trump, highest card of led suit wins.
Trick winner leads the next trick. Play is anticlockwise.
First team to win 7 tricks takes the hand (1 point). 7-0 sweep = 2 points (slam).
Hâkem stays if their team wins; otherwise rotates to the right.
Match is first team to 7 match points.

strategy.basic: As Hâkem, choose a trump suit where you have length and high cards (especially the Ace). Lead trump early to draw out opponents' trumps.
strategy.intermediate: Watch partner's signals. Discarding a specific suit hints at void or desire for that suit. As Hâkem, balance drawing trumps vs. saving them for later tricks.
strategy.advanced: Count all cards played, especially trumps. Communicate with partner through card choice. When Hâkem, calculate exactly how many trumps opponents hold before committing to a long suit play. Aim for Kot (all 13 tricks) when hand strength allows.
tips: Leading trumps early is a strong opening to establish dominance.
Track which Aces have been played — they decide many tricks.
If your partner leads a suit, support it by playing high if you're winning, or low to save high cards.
As Hâkem, a 5-card trump suit is usually the safest choice.

list.description: A bidding variant where players bid on how many tricks they can win. The highest bidder declares trump and must achieve their bid.

difficulty.easy: Follows suit but with poor trump management. Declares trump randomly.
difficulty.medium: Reasonable trump calling based on suit length. Basic partnership awareness.
difficulty.hard: Expert partnership play; counts every card, optimizes trump usage, aims for Kot (7-0 or 13-0). Communicates through card choice.

considerations: Anticlockwise game loop — affects lead advantage calculations.
Trump-calling logic based on initial 5-card distribution (suit length + high card density).
Partnership card counting and signaling (MCTS or similar is effective).
Hâkem rotation tracking for strategic play across hands.

phases.label: Select Hâkem
phases.notes: Deal cards face-up one at a time anticlockwise until a player receives an Ace. That player becomes Hâkem.

phases.label: Deal First 5 Cards
phases.notes: Player to Hâkem's right deals 5 cards to each player anticlockwise.

phases.label: Declare Trump (Hokm)
phases.notes: Hâkem examines 5 cards and declares the trump suit. Cannot show cards to anyone.

phases.label: Deal Remaining 8 Cards
phases.notes: Dealer deals remaining 8 cards to each player (5+8=13 total per player).

phases.label: Play 13 Tricks
phases.notes: Hâkem leads first trick. Play anticlockwise. Must follow suit. Highest trump wins; else highest of led suit. Winner leads next. Hand ends when a team reaches 7 tricks.

phases.label: Score Hand
phases.notes: Team with 7+ tricks scores 1 point. 7-0 slam = 2 points. Kot (all 13) = 3 points. Re-deal if match not over. Hâkem stays if team won, else rotates right.

edgeCases.text: If the Hâkem's team wins the hand, Hâkem stays for the next hand. If Hâkem's team loses, the player to Hâkem's right becomes the new Hâkem.
If a team wins all 7 tricks before the other team wins any (7-0), they score 2 points instead of 1.
Some variants: winning all 13 tricks (Kot) awards 3 points.
Once a team reaches 7 tricks, the hand ends immediately — remaining cards are not played.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Suits and ranks are as defined in the deck description above; no separate suit or rank set is used for this game.
engine.rankDescription: Ace (high) down to 2 (low) in all suits. Same ranking in trump and plain suits.
engine.dealPattern: Two-stage: 5 cards first (anticlockwise), Hâkem declares trump, then 8 more cards dealt
